label: Reading grade, hardest page
means: The school grade needed to read the hardest page; a lower grade is easier for everyone, so lower is better.
goal_source: goal: WCAG 2.2 Success Criterion 3.1.5 Reading Level (AAA) asks for text a reader with lower secondary education reads, seven to nine years of school (w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/reading-level, updated 2026-06-28, read 2026-11-10); grade 9 is its top. The near band is a Git Crafter default
source: state: Flesch-Kincaid grade of the main element's prose, params.key_pages at the widest of params.widths, via Playwright (Chrome)

label: Sentences over 30 words
means: Sentences on the pages that run too long to read easily; fewer is better.
goal_source: Git Crafter default goal: no sentence on a key page over params.long_sentence_words (30) words. GOV.UK splits sentences over 25 words (guidance.publishing.service.gov.uk, Use clear language, read 2026-11-10); 30 is the looser limit Git Crafter sets for its own writing
source: state: main element's prose, params.key_pages at the widest of params.widths, via Playwright (Chrome)

label: axe violations, not contrast
means: Page elements an automatic accessibility scan flags as hard for some people to use; fewer is better.
goal_source: goal: WCAG 2.2 AA as axe-core's default rules test it (w3.org/TR/WCAG22); the near band is a Git Crafter default
source: state: axe-core (the version installed in the repo, else beside the collectors) injected by Playwright (Chrome), params.key_pages at params.widths, all default rules but color-contrast and target-size

label: Small tap targets, phone width
means: Buttons and links on a phone that are too small to tap easily; fewer is better.
goal_source: goal: WCAG 2.2 AA, Success Criterion 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum), 24 by 24 CSS px (w3.org/TR/WCAG22); the near band is a Git Crafter default
source: state: axe-core target-size (switched on), params.key_pages at the narrowest of params.widths, under 768 px, via Playwright (Chrome)

label: Unlabeled form fields
means: Form fields with no label telling people what to type; fewer is better.
goal_source: goal: WCAG 2.2 AA, Success Criteria 3.3.2 Labels or Instructions and 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value (w3.org/TR/WCAG22); the near band is a Git Crafter default
source: state: Playwright (Chrome) on params.form_pages, loaded and never submitted

label: Broken internal links
means: Links inside the site that lead to a missing or failing page; fewer is better.
goal_source: Git Crafter default goal, no public benchmark: every internal link answers, since a dead link ends the visitor's task
source: state: GET crawl of the site from /, same origin, at most params.crawl_max fetches, params.crawl_skip never fetched

label: Main tasks done by keyboard alone
means: Main tasks a visitor finishes by keyboard: Tab reaches each link on the way, and Enter follows it to the next page.
goal_source: goal: every task, as WCAG 2.2 Success Criterion 2.1.1 Keyboard (Level A) requires all functionality to be operable through a keyboard interface (w3.org/TR/WCAG22, W3C Recommendation 2024-12-12, read 2026-11-04); the near band is a Git Crafter default
source: state: Playwright (Chrome) at 1280 px follows each task in params.tasks along its shortest route from / in the crawl, from a fresh load: on each page, Tab until the link that leads on has focus, then Enter, which must land on the next page. Tab stops when focus leaves the page or wraps; a task still unreached after 2,000 presses, or a page that fails to load, is named and not counted

label: Clicks from home, longest task
means: The most clicks from the home page that any main task needs; fewer is better.
goal_source: Git Crafter default goal, no public benchmark: every main task within two clicks of the home page. Nielsen Norman Group finds no data behind a click limit and weighs clear labels and fast pages beside it (nngroup.com/articles/3-click-rule, 2019-08-11, read 2026-11-10), so this tab pairs it with keyboard_task_share and words_before_action
source: state: shortest path from / in the crawled link graph to each task in params.tasks

label: Words before first action
means: Words a visitor reads before the first link or button, on the wordiest page; fewer is better.
goal_source: Git Crafter default goal, no public benchmark: a visitor reaches something to click within fifty words
source: state: visible words in main before its first link, button or field, params.key_pages at the widest of params.widths, via Playwright (Chrome)

label: TBT, mobile, slowest page
means: How long the slowest page freezes and ignores taps while loading on a phone; lower is better.
goal_source: goal: a Total Blocking Time under 200 ms on average mobile hardware (web.dev, Total Blocking Time, updated 2024-11-04, read 2026-11-04); near is 500 ms, above which web.dev rates INP poor, as TBT is INP's lab stand-in (web.dev, Interaction to Next Paint, updated 2025-09-02, read 2026-11-04)
source: latest: PageSpeed Insights API v5, strategy=mobile, lab TBT, params.key_pages; a page PSI cannot answer, and every page of a built static site, is measured by our own Playwright lab run under Lighthouse's mobile settings and marked (lab)

label: Form page KiB, heaviest form
means: How much data a visitor downloads to open the heaviest form, where most tasks end; lower is better.
goal_source: goal: Lighthouse total-byte-weight guidance, aim below 1,600 KiB; Lighthouse flags pages over 5,000 KiB (developer.chrome.com/docs/lighthouse/performance/total-byte-weight, read 2026-11-03), applied to the pages where tasks finish
source: state: Playwright (Chrome) network log, all responses at load, each of params.form_pages at 1280 px in a fresh context; value is the heaviest form page
